preamble: Click loss in East Kalahari Khoe (Shua and Tshwa clusters: Cara, ǀXaise, Danisi, Deti, Kua, Tsua). Here the palatal click series of Proto-Kalahari Khoe has been replaced throughout by non-click palatal consonants, a regular sound change documented by Traill & Vossen (1997). Sands & Gunnink (2019) note that Khoe click loss increases with distance from the Kalahari core and may be sped up by contact with languages that lack clicks. Western languages such as ǀGwi and Kxoe, and conservative Ts'ixa, keep the click, e.g. ǀGwi ǂéē, Ts'ixa ǂé 'ear'. The plain and aspirated-fricative palatal clicks *ǂ and *ǂx became the alveolo-palatal affricate [tɕ] in Cara, ǀXaise, Danisi and Deti, and also in Kua and Tsua before u and in *ǂx. Before back vowels, Kua and Tsua instead have [kʲ] (see click_palatal_to_k_palatalized). Like the replacement of ǃ by velars, this keeps the click's front (palatal) release place without the velaric airstream. Forms follow the GLD's transcription (Vossen 1997 data). In that system ɕ and ʓ are alveolo-palatal affricates [tɕ, dʑ], y is [j], and ʸ marks palatalization.
